- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The ruling in Furman v. Georgia (1972) struck down the death penalty as it was applied at the time, leading to a temporary moratorium on the death penalty in the U.S.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In Graham v. Florida (2010), the court held that it was unconstitutional to sentence a juvenile offender to life without parole for a non-homicide offense.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In Miller v. Alabama (2012), the court ruled that mandatory life without parole sentences for juveniles were unconstitutional.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Supreme Court's interpretation of the Eighth Amendment has helped reduce the use of the death penalty and provided protections for juvenile offenders.
